problem: Object-goal navigation agents in unfamiliar environments need good visual representations and robust policies, but existing methods use limited object-relationship modeling and suffer from non-discriminative rewards, leading to deadlocks such as looping or getting stuck.
motivation: An agent must find a target object from first-person observations without a map. Modeling object relationships (category proximity, spatial correlation) under episode context should improve representations, while imitation from experts with a dynamic reward should give more informative guidance than sparse environment rewards.
key_idea: Combine a context-aware graph inference module (TransH-based object relationship inference guided by image, action and memory contexts) with a GAIL-learned dynamic reward added to the environment reward to train a more robust object-goal navigation policy.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited. The abstract claims that the two components are complementary: CGI improves visual representation and GAIL addresses non-discriminative rewards, and both help the agent escape deadlock states.
method: Context-aware graph inference (CGI): integrates object relationships (category proximity and spatial correlation) into visual representation learning.
TransH relation inference: uses translation on hyperplane to infer context-aware object relationships.
Multi-context guidance: image, action and memory contexts over the navigation episode guide the relation inference.
GAIL: adversarial imitation learning from expert demonstrations to learn a discriminator-based reward.
Dynamic reward combination: the GAIL dynamic reward is combined with environment rewards to address non-discriminative reward and guide the policy.

setting.backbone: not specified in abstract (RL/IL-trained navigation policy with graph-based visual representation)
setting.training_data: Expert demonstrations for GAIL plus RL interaction in AI2-THOR/RoboTHOR; scale not stated in abstract

results: The abstract claims the method significantly improves effectiveness and efficiency of navigation in unfamiliar environments on AI2-THOR and RoboTHOR. No numbers or baselines are given in the abstract.
